scope: Fictional native-research telemetry only; common oracle for both backends. No account identity, host identity, broker account/order, protected data or real trading path is a fixture input.

cases.action: Ingest all events through the arm's native OTel path; retrieve every native usage category for each receipt
Replay success-a twice with the identical receipt_id
Restart only this run's owned Collector, then replay/query the frozen events
Restart only this run's owned backend and query persisted logs plus a pre-restart historical metric sample
Query fixture-a and fixture-b scopes separately and exercise a research worker's denial of broker execution authority

Use pinned common restic and an isolated baseline repository for owned live telemetry and fictional SQLite: quiesce/checkpoint, seal hashes, backup, check --read-data, restore --verify into empty independent target, restart restored services and query the same oracle. No rest-server is required for backend qualification.
Use upstream UI in an isolated browser: open the fixture-a dashboard and locate failed receipt with matching log/metric/trace. Check every declared panel and query fixture-b separately.
Induce frozen failed worker event; exercise native routing to isolated common ntfy, restart owned notification components and replay identical event.
Pinned Dagu/native process control launches fictional successful and failed jobs, interrupts an owned child, then inspects completion/restart and cleanup records.
Score retained recovery mechanisms on disposable off-host stores independently; do not use these results as a telemetry backend gate.

oracle.attack_boundary: Research-client backup identity has no destination admin/snapshot rights. All attacks use disposable seeded stores on an independent owned destination.
oracle.protected_expected: Both client attacks are refused; seeded source hashes/snapshots stay intact; check --read-data and fresh-target restore --verify exit 0 with byte-identical fixture state.
oracle.sftp_expected: Both attacks succeed on disposable writable SFTP. Use separately seeded attack and restore stores; destructive control success is not restoration qualification.
oracle.private_repository_isolation: Two fictional principals cannot read/write/delete each other repository; TLS identity is verified with no plaintext fallback.
oracle.destination_identity: Retain independent-host and persistent-path proof privately; publish scoped redacted attestation and fictional hashes only.
oracle.live_state: Quiesce owned fixture, flush/checkpoint fictional SQLite, seal public hash manifest, back up, close source, restore into empty independent target, restart restored services and query the same oracle.
